title: Walk the folders of the builder
prompt:
# Story 2: Walk the folders of the builder

- **Story**: XXX-walk-builder-folders
- **Created**: 2026-11-07
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: open the workspace, open `drivers` and `adrs` and see their files, open the two other folders and see that they are not
  built yet.

## Story

As a team member, I want to open and close the folders of the tree and see which drivers and ADRs my project has, so that I know what
exists and where each file lives.

## Acceptance tests

Opening and closing

- [ ] **Given** a closed folder, **When** the user presses its row (or uses Enter or Space on it), **Then** it opens, its chevron points
  down, and its row has `aria-expanded="true"`. **When** the user presses it again, **Then** it closes.
- [ ] **Given** the four folders, **Then** each opens and closes on its own, and several can be open at once.
- [ ] **Given** folders that are open, **When** a file is opened and closed (stories 3 and 4), **Then** they are as they were.
- [ ] **Given** folders that are open, **When** the workspace is closed and opened again, **Then** they are all closed.

The folders

- [ ] **Given** a folder row, **Then** it shows the chevron, the folder icon, the name (cut with "..." when long) and, on the right, a count.
- [ ] **Given** the rows `drivers` and `adrs`, **Then** each also shows a small lock with the label "Read-only". The other two do not.
- [ ] **Given** `drivers`, **Then** its count is the number of drivers the project has: the five fixed ones, written or not, plus the ones the
  team added. **Given** `adrs`, **Then** its count is the number of ADRs. **Given** `architectural-enablers` and `stories`, **Then** each
  shows how many the project holds.

`drivers`

- [ ] **Given** `drivers` is open, **Then** it lists one file per driver: first the five fixed ones, in this order,
  `core-functionality.md`, `architectural-concerns.md`, `constraints.md`, `quality-attributes.md`, `design-purpose.md`, then the ones the
  team added, in the order they were added, as `<identity>.md`.
- [ ] **Given** a driver that has no text yet, **Then** it is listed all the same.
- [ ] **Given** a file row, **Then** it shows an icon of the kind, the file name cut with "..." when long, and, as a tooltip, the driver's name
  ("Core Functionality").

`adrs`

- [ ] **Given** `adrs` is open, **Then** it lists one file per ADR, in order of number, with the file name as it is in the repository, for
  example `0011-use-typescript-for-the-frontend.md`, and, as a tooltip, "ADR 0011. Use TypeScript for the frontend".
- [ ] **Given** the project has no ADR, **Then** `adrs` shows the italic line "No ADRs yet." when it is open.
- [ ] **Given** ADRs of any status (Proposed, Accepted, Deprecated, Superseded), **Then** all of them are listed.

`architectural-enablers` and `stories`

- [ ] **Given** one of these two folders, **When** it is opened, **Then** it shows, instead of files, the italic line "Coming in another
  story.", and closes again as any folder.
- [ ] **Given** the tree, **Then** it has no button to create a story, an enabler or a theme, no diagram button, no rename, and nothing can
  be dragged or dropped.

Immutable

- [ ] **Given** a file or a folder of `drivers` or `adrs`, **Then** the tree has no way to create, rename, move, delete or change it: a double
  click, F2, a drag, a right click and Delete do nothing to it.

Keeping up with the project

- [ ] **Given** a driver was added on the Drivers page, or an ADR on the ADR page, **When** the user opens the workspace, **Then** the tree
  lists it, and the counts are right.
- [ ] **Given** two projects, **Then** each shows its own drivers and ADRs.

## Business rules and constraints

- The tree only shows what the project has. It never writes anything.
- A file's path is its path in the repository, relative to the folder of BWYN there: `drivers/<identity>.md` and
  `adrs/<number>-<slug>.md`.
- The five fixed drivers are always listed, written or not, because they are part of every project. A driver the team removed is not.
- `architectural-enablers` and `stories` are placeholders. Their count is the number of items the project holds, but the items are not
  listed, opened or acted on until their own stories.

## Out of scope

- Opening a file (stories 3 and 4).
- Listing, opening, creating, editing, moving, linking or deleting anything in `architectural-enablers` and `stories`, themes, and the
  prompt.
- Writing drivers and ADRs (their own pages), and a search or a filter in the tree.

## Tasks

- [ ] Describe the four folders once (key, name, kind, whether locked), and draw the tree from that list.
- [ ] Draw the folder row (chevron, icon, name, lock, count) with open and close by click, Enter and Space, and keep what is open for as
  long as the workspace is.
- [ ] List the drivers (the five fixed, then the added ones) and the ADRs (by number) as file rows, with their file name and tooltip.
- [ ] Show "No ADRs yet." for an empty `adrs`, and "Coming in another story." inside the two folders that are not built.
- [ ] Count the items of each folder.
- [ ] Take out of the tree the themes, the dragging, the "New theme" and "New story" buttons and everything that edits (see the Reference).
- [ ] Test: the order and the counts, the five fixed drivers with no text, an empty `adrs`, and that nothing in `drivers` or `adrs` reacts to
  double click, F2 or drag.

tasks.text: Define a static folder-descriptor array (key, display name, kind, lock flag, placeholder text) in the `ui` layer and derive the tree from it (ADR-0007, Principle: Declarative over imperative)
Implement the `BuilderTreeViewModel` in the `interface-adapters` layer, exposing folder open/closed state, item lists for `drivers` and `adrs`, and counts for all four folders (ADR-0007)
Bind `BuilderTreeViewModel` in the Inversify composition root; inject the existing driver and ADR query use cases (ADR-0006)
Build the `FolderRow` React component: chevron, folder icon, name with overflow ellipsis, optional lock badge, count; toggle on click, Enter, and Space; set `aria-expanded` (ADR-0005)
Build the `FileRow` React component: file icon, file name with overflow ellipsis, tooltip with display name (ADR-0005)
Render `drivers` file list: five fixed drivers first in specified order, then team-added drivers in creation order, each as `<identity>.md`
Render `adrs` file list: ADRs in ascending number order; show italic "No ADRs yet." when the list is empty; include all statuses
Render `architectural-enablers` and `stories` with italic "Coming in another story." placeholder when open; omit all create/rename/drag controls
Suppress all mutation interactions on `drivers` and `adrs` rows: double-click, F2, drag, right-click context menu, and Delete key do nothing
Reset all folder open/closed state to closed when the workspace is closed
Write Jest unit tests for `BuilderTreeViewModel`: correct order and counts for drivers (including unwritten fixed drivers), empty-ADR case, multi-project isolation (ADR-0005)
Write Jest unit tests for `FolderRow` and `FileRow`: aria attributes, truncation, lock badge presence/absence, tooltip content
Verify the full frontend build and test suite completes within the ten-minute budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build)
